blips.name: Plant 3D
blips.description: AutoCAD Plant 3D is a specialized 3D computer-aided design (CAD) software developed by Autodesk for designing, modeling, and documenting process plants, such as oil and gas facilities, chemical plants, water treatment systems, and food and beverage manufacturing units. It is built directly on the familiar AutoCAD platform and included as part of standard AutoCAD subscriptions.

blips.name: Common data environment (ISO 19650)
blips.description: A single, controlled place for project information, run to the ISO 19650 workflow (work in progress, shared, published, archived). It is the default for all new projects.

blips.name: Autodesk Construction Cloud
blips.description: Cloud platform for document control, model coordination and site workflows in one place. Being trialled on two projects as a common data environment.

blips.name: Generative AI for document review
blips.description: Using AI assistants to summarise specifications, check submittals against requirements and draft responses. Promising, but outputs still need full human review.

blips.name: Dynamo
blips.description: Visual programming for Revit, used to automate repetitive modelling tasks and design checks. A standard part of the design team's toolkit.

blips.name: Grasshopper
blips.description: Visual programming for Rhino, suited to complex geometry and design option studies. Useful alongside Revit on facade and structural form-finding work.

blips.name: Drone surveys and photogrammetry
blips.description: Regular drone flights produce site models for progress tracking, volume calculations and as-built checks. Moved to Trial after successful use on three sites.

blips.name: Offsite modular construction
blips.description: Manufacturing building elements or whole modules in a factory, then assembling them on site. Can cut programme time and waste; needs design for manufacture and assembly from the start.

blips.name: Forma Site Design
blips.description: Forma Site Design (formerly known as Autodesk Forma and originally developed by Spacemaker) is a cloud-based, AI-powered software platform built for early-stage urban planning, conceptual design, and site analysis.

blips.name: COBie asset data handover
blips.description: Structured asset information handed to the client in COBie format, so maintenance teams get usable data rather than boxes of manuals.

blips.name: Digital twins for operations
blips.description: Connecting the as-built model to live sensor and maintenance data, so clients can run the asset from a digital replica. Worth exploring with clients who have the data maturity.
